results.requirement: Cursor-left and erase-to-end preserve preceding text.
UTF-8 decoding preserves an accented scalar and a two-cell CJK character.
A combining mark in a later feed extends the prior cell without advancing the cursor.
A wide character at the last column wraps with a continuation cell.
Narrowing reflows a logical line and preserves the cursor.
Narrowing preserves explicit hard line boundaries.
Scrolling preserves ordered history separately from the active screen.
Leaving alternate screen restores primary text and saved cursor.
Nebulax requires woman-technologist to occupy one two-cell grapheme; the following ASCII character starts at column 2.
Under the proposed grapheme policy, thumbs-up plus skin tone is one two-cell cluster even when the modifier arrives later.
A US regional-indicator pair is stored as one two-cell grapheme, not two independently editable scalar cells.
Heart followed by VS16 becomes a two-cell emoji, including when the selector arrives later.
Watch followed by VS15 uses the proposed one-cell text-presentation policy; this is an explicit width policy, not a Unicode segmentation mandate.
A fully-qualified keycap sequence is one two-cell grapheme under the proposed emoji-width policy.
BS moves one cell, then ECH clears both the base and its attached combining mark.
After a two-cell emoji and ASCII suffix, BS plus EL removes only the suffix and keeps the intact cluster.
CR plus ECH(2) clears a complete two-cell ZWJ cluster; no component may remain at a later column.
A two-cell ZWJ grapheme fits exactly after three ASCII cells in a five-column row; only the suffix wraps.
A two-cell ZWJ grapheme plus ASCII fits in four columns after resize; components stay attached.
